author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: The veterinarian directory, in both its page form and its machine-readable form, can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty. The choice is made in the page's address, matches the whole specialty name ignoring letter case, and survives page links.
acceptance_criteria: Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is narrowed to it, then only those veterinarians are listed, a page at a time.
Given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable directory is narrowed to it, then it carries only those veterinarians.
Given a narrowed directory spanning more than one page, when a page link is followed, then the same specialty still applies.
Given a specialty name differing from the held name only by letter case, when the directory is narrowed to it, then it matches.
Given a name matching the start of a held specialty but not the whole of it, when the directory is narrowed to it, then no veterinarian matches.
Given a specialty name no veterinarian holds, when the directory is narrowed to it, then both forms are returned normally with no veterinarians rather than refused.
Given a specialty chosen as nothing or as spaces alone, when either form is opened, then it behaves as though none had been chosen.
Given no specialty chosen, when either form of the directory is opened, then every veterinarian is listed exactly as before this change.
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any page control for choosing the specialty (NG-10)
narrowing the directory by any attribute other than specialty
notes: Owner-stated surface contract (2026-08-08): an optional `specialty` parameter in the address of both vet list surfaces, and pagination links that carry it. REQ-VET-003 reinstates the machine-readable directory as a supported surface and needs no code change; its acceptance bullet is met by behavior already shipped, so it gets no slice of its own. Two questions were recorded in the PRD Open Questions rather than settled here: no consumer is named for the machine-readable directory, and nothing on the page names the specialty in force.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Narrow non-goal NG-9: free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows (specialty) is in scope. Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the existing vet feature package with no new package, type, or layer. It is the paged-derived-query pattern already shown by OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith plus OwnerController.processFindForm, applied to Vet.specialties.name; the adjustment is one repository query method per surface, one request parameter per controller method, and parameterized pagination links in the template. Contracts table rows for VetRepository and VetController keep their shape; only their Implements sets gain REQ-VET-004 once the behavior ships, which is doc-sync work after the slice, not before it. Basis: grep over the vet package and OwnerRepository/OwnerController (the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker resolution basis).
integration_points: VetRepository gains a paged finder over the specialty name for /vets.html and an unpaged finder for /vets; the property path is specialties.name via Vet.specialties and Specialty extends NamedEntity
VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each gain an optional specialty request parameter and branch to the filtered finder only when the normalized value is non-blank
vetList.html pagination links gain the specialty parameter; the model gains the normalized specialty value for the links to read
No change to Vet, Vets, Specialty, the schema, the seed data, or CacheConfiguration

patterns.description: paged Spring Data derived query taking the search term plus a Pageable; the vet finder is the same shape with the IgnoreCase keyword and no StartingWith, giving whole-name case-insensitive equality in one keyword

blank-parameter normalization: null becomes empty, then strip. Reuse the normalization, not the branch that follows it -- owner search rejects a no-match with a notFound binding error, and this slice must return the normal page or JSON with an empty vet list instead

pagination links are hand-concatenated query strings today. Build them with the parameterized link expression form @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=...)} so Thymeleaf URL-encodes the caller-supplied value and omits it when null; concatenation would neither encode nor omit

risks.risk: Annotating the new finders @Cacheable("vets") would key an unbounded cache on caller-supplied text, letting any client grow it without limit. The vets cache declares no size limit and no eviction (CacheConfiguration; Open Questions item 5)
risks.mitigation: Leave the filtered finders uncached. The unfiltered findAll paths keep their existing annotations

risks.risk: Reproducing the PostgreSQL case-sensitivity defect that owner search carries, where matching depends on column collation and differs per vendor
risks.mitigation: Use the Spring Data IgnoreCase keyword so the case fold is expressed in the generated query, identical on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL. Do not rely on collation or on schema changes

risks.risk: The specialty value is a new untrusted input reflected into page hrefs
risks.mitigation: Parameterized link expressions URL-encode it; Thymeleaf escapes th:href output; NG-10 keeps it off the page as text. The value reaches JPA only through a parameterized derived query

risks.risk: Joining the eager ManyToMany could duplicate root rows and corrupt the page count
risks.mitigation: A vet holds each specialty at most once (Set plus the join-table key), so the join yields one row per matching vet. A test over a vet with several specialties confirms it

notes: Two points the prd-entry leaves open, taken at the narrowest reading consistent with the owner's contract. First, /vets stays unpaged: the non_goals list bars paging the machine-readable directory, so its finder returns a Collection and the Vets wrapper is filled as today. Second, the model attribute carrying the value for the pagination links is the normalized (stripped) specialty, so a blank value yields links identical to today's. No ADR: the product decisions are already recorded in the 2026-08-08 directory-filter ADR, and the two constraints above are local and reversible. One durable-memory correction landed with this triage -- docs/system-design.md Known Defects carried a row calling the machine-readable vet route an artifact pending removal, which REQ-VET-003 has made false; the row is removed and the settled paragraph now states the current status with an ADR back-link. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: the caller-supplied specialty reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived finders findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String[, Pageable]) in VetRepository. Derived queries bind the argument as a JPA parameter; no string concatenation, no @Query fragment, no Sort/Pageable property name derived from input. The int page parameter is bound by type, not interpolated. No SQL/JPQL injection path.

Unbounded-cache constraint holds: both new finders carry @Transactional(readOnly = true) and no @Cacheable. Verified against CacheConfiguration, which creates the vets cache from a bare MutableConfiguration with statistics only, so no size limit and no eviction policy. Only findAll() and findAll(Pageable) keep @Cacheable("vets"), and both take no caller-supplied key material, so a client cannot grow the cache via /vets?specialty=<random>.

Reflected-XSS on the HTML page: the specialty model attribute is emitted only inside th:href parameterized link expressions, @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}. Thymeleaf URL-encodes the parameter value in that form and then HTML-escapes the attribute output, so metacharacters (" < > space) cannot break the attribute or the URL. The link base is a fixed literal path, so no javascript:-scheme or host-control injection is reachable. Template sweep for the escaping class found no th:utext, no th:inline, and no remaining hand-concatenated href carrying a caller-supplied value in vetList.html; the surviving __${...}__ preprocessing sites (ownersList.html, ownerDetails.html, layout.html) interpolate only integers or server-side literals, none of them this slice's parameter.

Reflected-XSS on the JSON document: /vets echoes no request value. showResourcesVetList returns only the Vets aggregate; the specialty is used as a query argument and never serialized into the response, so there is no reflected sink in either representation.

Filter is read-only and adds no authorization surface: both handlers are GET, both finders are readOnly, and the filtered result set is a subset of what the unfiltered directory already publishes. No new data is exposed and no privilege boundary is crossed.

Blank-input normalization is fail-closed in the safe direction: chosenSpecialty() maps null, empty, and whitespace-only to null, which routes to the pre-existing unfiltered path rather than issuing a query on an empty string, and makes the template emit exactly the pre-filter links (no stray bare specialty= parameter).

Supply chain: the change set touches no build file (build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle/ all unchanged), adds no dependency, and introduces no new transitive surface, so this pass brings no new CVE exposure. No dependencyCheck plugin is configured in this project, so dependencyCheckAnalyze was not available to run.

No secrets: swept the changed vet surface and the diff for credential-shaped material (password, secret, token, api key, and connection-string forms). Nothing hardcoded; the slice introduces no credential, no external call, and no new configuration key.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The comment above `model.addAttribute("specialty", chosenSpecialty)` says the null value makes the pagination links 'omit the parameter entirely rather than carrying an empty one.' That is the mechanism the design-block explicitly disproved: Thymeleaf renders a null-valued parameter in a parameterized link expression as a bare `specialty=`, it does not omit it. The template avoids that exact outcome by branching on a `th:with="filtered=${specialty != null}"` flag between two separate link expressions (vetList.html:27-31), which is the opposite of relying on omission. `docs/system-design.md` § Contracts > Views now states the correct (non-omission) fact for the next filter-carrying template, but this controller comment still tells a colder reader the false version, next to the very code that had to work around it.
findings.fix: Rewrite the comment to state why the model carries null rather than an empty string: e.g. 'Null, not an empty string, so the template's `specialty != null` check in vetList.html can tell "no specialty chosen" from "chosen and blank" (blank is normalized away above) and select the unfiltered link expression.'

findings.description: The three new `private static final String` specialty constants (HELD_SPECIALTY, UNHELD_SPECIALTY, SPECIALTY_NEEDING_ENCODING) are declared between the `james()`/`helen()` fixture-builder methods (lines 64-83) and `@BeforeEach setup()` (line 91), interrupting the class's method flow with a field block. Every other field in the class (mockMvc, vets) is declared at the top. A cold reader scanning for state has to look in two places.

author: test-reviewer
recommendations: The blank/whitespace-normalization rule (VetController.chosenSpecialty) is a pure String->String function with no I/O, but it is private and exercised only through MockMvc requests (theBlankSpecialtyChoiceShouldBehaveAsNoChoice and its JSON-endpoint twin). Per testing-principles.md Test Pyramid, a new controller rule that could be tested without booting the framework belongs in a unit test at the base of the pyramid; extracting it to a package-private, independently-testable method (or a small value type) would let a fast unit test cover the stripping/blank/null branches directly instead of only via the web layer. Not blocking - the current tests do exercise all three branches (null, blank, real value) and VetController shows 100% branch coverage per jacocoTestReport - but it is exactly the drift the brief asks reviewers to flag.

No adversarial/special-character coverage for the specialty parameter (e.g. control characters, very long strings, an ampersand or other URL-metacharacter value beyond the existing space-encoding case). Low risk here since Spring Data derived queries are parameterized (no injection surface) and Thymeleaf's @{} link-builder URL-encodes automatically, but a single @ParameterizedTest/@CsvSource case exercising a value with '&' or non-ASCII characters would close the boundary-testing checklist item cheaply.
approved_aspects: ClinicServiceTests' four new tests run against the real H2 fixture data (data.sql) rather than invented data, and correctly target the EAGER @ManyToMany join-duplication risk: filtering on 'dentistry' (held once by Douglas, who also holds 'surgery') would surface Hibernate's classic pagination-with-eager-collection duplicate-row bug if present, and the test proves it does not (getTotalElements()==1, single row).
Whole-name vs. prefix-match distinction (edge case 3) and case-insensitivity are each given a dedicated, correctly-named test at the repository level.

VetControllerTests covers both surfaces (/vets.html and /vets), the empty-result-is-200 case, the blank-value-as-absent case, the absent-parameter case, and both pagination-link scenarios (parameter carried and URL-encoded vs. parameter omitted when unfiltered) - matching every PRD acceptance criterion and edge case for REQ-VET-004.
Test data follows the three-tier naming convention (HELD_SPECIALTY, UNHELD_SPECIALTY, SPECIALTY_NEEDING_ENCODING with a comment explaining its role); no mystery literals.
Test names follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school from testing-principles.md.
VetController.java shows 100% instruction and branch coverage in the jacoco report after this change.
./gradlew test passes cleanly for both modified test files.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty

blast_radius.note: Nine files, 41 hunks, no sensitive paths, and every code edit lands inside the vet feature package plus its one template. The only reach outside the slice's own surface is the pre-existing /vets JSON route gaining an optional parameter, which is additive: with the parameter absent both handlers take the identical unfiltered path they took before, and the unfiltered pagination links render byte-identically.

semantic_surprise.note: Behavior matches its description exactly - no inverted condition, blank normalization consistent across both handlers, filtered and unfiltered paths cleanly separated - but the safety rationale the diff writes into VetRepository javadoc and into system-design.md does not hold for the code beside it. The new finders are left uncached because, in the javadoc's words, keying the cache on a caller-supplied name would let any client grow it without bound. Yet the retained findAll(Pageable) keeps its Cacheable annotation on the same vets cache, and its cache key is the PageRequest built from the caller's own unvalidated page parameter, in a Caffeine JCache created from a bare MutableConfiguration with no size limit and no eviction. So a request to /vets.html with an arbitrary page number already grows that cache without bound - the exact shape this slice declares unacceptable - while the slice's docs narrow Open Question 5 to the unfiltered read methods in a way that reads as settled. Second, smaller: vetList.html line 20 iterates a loop variable named specialty over vet.specialties, while the new model attribute is also named specialty and holds a String rather than a Specialty. The two scopes do not overlap, so rendering is correct today, but one template now carries one name for two types.

test_adequacy.note: The tests would fail against a broken implementation rather than restate it. ClinicServiceTests runs against real H2 seed data and targets the actual risk of the change: filtering on dentistry for a vet who also holds surgery proves the collection join does not duplicate the row or inflate the page count, and separate tests pin whole-name-versus-prefix matching and case insensitivity. VetControllerTests covers both surfaces, the empty result as 200 rather than a refusal, blank-as-absent on each handler, and both link-rendering branches including the URL-encoded space. Every acceptance criterion in the prd-entry record maps to a named test.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round two is unanimous approval from the full four-reviewer roster the plan dispatched, and the round-one findings were re-verified individually rather than waved through. But the security approval certifies the caching mitigation on a false premise - that findAll() and findAll(Pageable) both take no caller-supplied key material - which is wrong for findAll(Pageable), whose key is the caller's page number. Its conclusion about the specialty parameter still holds, so this is a weakened certification on exactly the question worth checking, not an incorrect verdict. The test-reviewer also carried two recommendations forward unaddressed, both explicitly non-blocking betterments.

scope_deviation.note: The docs footprint is wide for one filter - a reinstated requirement, a narrowed non-goal, a new non-goal, an ADR, and Contracts-table corrections - but every piece traces to an owner decision quoted verbatim in the ADR and recorded in the prd-entry scope. The code stays within the design-block's declared paths. The one design revision and the quality-gate abort were a doc-ownership coverage gap and a withdrawn deferral of the Implements cells, both resolved by superseding records, not a wander past the triaged surface.

rationale: Behavior is correct and well tested. What deserves a look is the cache rationale this change writes into durable docs: the new finders are uncached to stop a caller growing an eviction-free cache, yet the retained paged findAll is keyed on the caller's own page number and does exactly that. Read VetRepository against CacheConfiguration before merging.
